heading: 14.6 Type checking rules
text:
### 14.6 Type checking rules [LUNI.14.6]

**Valid.** `complex <unit>` supports `+` / `-` with another `complex
<unit>` of the same unit (preserves the unit), `+` / `-` with a bare
`<unit>` value (a real-component shift), and `*` with a bare `Float`
(scalar scaling, preserves the unit). `abs()` returns the scalar
magnitude in `<unit>`; `arg()` returns `radian`; `conjugate()` returns
`complex <unit>`.

**Refused** ([LUNI.8.4]): `complex <unit> * complex <unit>` and
`complex <unit> / complex <unit>` are compile errors.

**No ordering on complex — compile error.** `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` are
rejected; authors compare `abs()`, `real()`, or `imag()` instead. `==`
and `!=` are valid (component-wise equality).
